module_name: Data Collection via Official APIs (X API v2, TikTok Research API, YouTube Data API, Reddit API, Bluesky AT Protocol)
module_description: Module 4 is hands-on API collection: authentication, query operators, pagination, rate limits, and quota budgeting, plus honest treatment of access politics after 2023-2026 (X academic access removed, Meta gated, Bluesky open). Students learn to build a defensible sampling frame (top vs recent, keyword vs full archive) and to archive what they collect.
core_concepts: Authentication and authorization models (OAuth2, bearer, app password)
Query operators and endpoint design (search, timeline, video list, comments)
Sampling frames: keyword, timeline, snowball, random
learning_outcomes: C3 Use at least three platform APIs to collect a documented sample
C4 Justify a sampling frame and quantify its bias
C5 Evaluate API access cost and quota against a research budget
methods_models: REST/JSON collection, cursor pagination, time-window slicing, quota budgeting, snapshot archiving
Common learning-by-building: one API per lab, output CSV + collection log
evaluation_metrics: Not quantified by ML metrics; assessed by completeness of collection log and reproducibility of counts
pitfalls_limitations: Silent query truncation, timezone bugs, deleted/edited content, deduplication across windows, undisclosed API filters
tools_stack: requests/httpx, tweepy or raw X API v2 calls, praw (Reddit), google-api-python-client (YouTube), atproto or requests for Bluesky Jetstream
commercial_platforms: Side-by-side quota comparison across tiers (X basic/pro/enterprise vs free research tools)
tools_access_cost: X moved academic access to paid tiers after 2023; Meta Content Library is free but institutionally gated; SOMAR-type research environments began charging research teams from 2026 (about USD 371/team/month per public reporting)
lab_activities: Collect the same topic from 3 platforms with a written collection log (query, dates, counts, filters)
datasets_apis: X recent search + Bluesky firehose sample + YouTube comments on a topic; plus Reddit sample
assessment_methods: Written analysis/design document plus a short quiz; graded on correctness of concepts and quality of justification
data_collection_workflow: Define the question -> choose platform and access route -> collect via API or permitted scrape -> archive raw with checksums -> clean and document schema -> analyse -> preserve dataset and code
textbooks: Russell, Mining the Social Web, API chapters
Exploratory Tutorials for Data Analysis (API/SQL chapters)
trends_2024_2026: 2024-2026: access became the main constraint; curriculum must teach quota literacy and teach Bluesky/open protocol as the fallback research surface
industry_relevance: Social media analyst, market-insights researcher, and data-journalist roles; this module is used for social listening, brand/issue monitoring, and audience research, and is referenced by industry certifications such as Meta Blueprint, Hootsuite Social Marketing, and Google Analytics.
localization_context: Taught with Indonesian-language material (IndoBERT/IndoRoBERTa/NusaBERT, InSet lexicon, Indonesian social datasets) so students can reproduce the analysis on local corpora; comparisons are made against Anglocentric benchmarks whose labels often transfer poorly.
ethics_regulation: Platform Terms of Service, UU PDP No. 27/2022 (Indonesian personal data protection), GDPR for EU-origin data, and IRB-style review for any data involving private individuals; public is not the same as consentable for social data.
case_study_scenarios: Collect one month of an issue's discussion within a fixed budget and defend the sample.
deliverable_format: Documented dataset (raw JSON + tidy CSV) + collection log
